events.statement: The redis-cache dataset loss is explained by a failover/promotion with a COLD (empty) new primary. At 2026-04-09T13:22:10Z ERROR 'node redis-cache-2 failed health check (3 consecutive PING timeouts); marking primary as down' is immediately followed at 13:22:52Z by WARN 'failover: promoting replica redis-cache-3 to primary; dataset on new primary is empty (replica was resyncing)'. The promoted node was still resyncing, so it holds no quote keyspace.

There is NO process-restart signature: a contains='Ready to accept connections' search over 12:00-14:00Z returned total_matched 0 (partial:false, data_range 09:00-14:59Z). Restart-count delta in 13:15-13:35Z is therefore 0 process restarts; the only topology event is 1 primary->replica promotion (redis-cache-2 -> redis-cache-3). So this is failover/promotion, NOT a process restart.

Post-promotion recovery is visible as replica resync and a client reconnect storm: WARN 'MASTER <-> REPLICA sync started (full resync) for redis-cache-2' at 13:28:42Z (again 13:35:26Z) and WARN 'client reconnect storm: 15048 new connections in 10s' at 13:30:20Z (29623 at 13:35:30Z) — consistent with clients failing over to the new (cold) primary and rebuilding.

redis-cache connected_clients shows the client-connection loss at the exact failover minute in 120s buckets: 312.88 avg at 13:20, collapses to 41.8 at 13:22 and 38.77 at 13:24 (min 37.15), then recovers to 307.88 by 13:26 — the ~4-minute loss of connections is the failover/resync window and matches the promotion timeline.

events.answer: The redis-cache dataset loss at ~13:22Z was caused by a FAILOVER/PRIMARY PROMOTION, not a process restart or external flush: the old primary redis-cache-2 was marked down after 3 consecutive PING timeouts (13:22:10Z), and redis-cache-3 was promoted to primary with an EMPTY dataset because the replica "was resyncing" (13:22:52Z) — so the new primary came up cold, which is exactly what produced hit_ratio 97%->10%, memory 74%->6%, the ~4-min connected_clients collapse, and the downstream miss storm/quote latency. events.title: Shared redis-cache primary failover promoted an empty (resyncing) replica, causing a quote-key miss storm that starved market-data-service and blew pricing-engine's quote deadline
Capacity saturation on the market-data-service/redis-cache quote path from market-data volume, with no faulty change
External dependency failure: exchange-gateway/exchange-api degradation bloats snapshot rebuilds
Unrecorded config/feature-flag or routing change to a pricing-engine dependency
Reporter-adjacent change hypothesis: auth-service dep-5604 (Session cookie hardening) affected pricing

events.summary: H1 is adequately proven and all rivals are contradicted by measured evidence. Every hop of the causal chain now rests on verified findings: (1) the load-bearing first hop is directly observed — redis hit_ratio 96.34%->10.45% and memory_pct 74.63%->6.0% in the same 13:22 bucket, evictions flat ~2-4/min, no maxmemory ceiling, no FLUSHALL/config-reset (F19/F20/F22/F34/F35/F41); (2) the mechanism my round-2 review flagged as the last unverified hop is now a verbatim log signature, not inference — PING-timeout health-check failure 13:22:10Z, then promotion of redis-cache-3 with 'dataset on new primary is empty (replica was resyncing)' 13:22:52Z, with 0 process restarts and 1 promotion (F37/F38); (3) downstream propagation is co-located in the 13:22 minute across miss-storm WARNs (F16/F32), MDS p99 step from baseline (F31/F33), and pricing-engine p99 step to 2225ms with the single error signature naming MDS while pricing-engine CPU stays flat ~39-40% (F13/F14/F17/F18). Temporal order is tight: onset bounded to the 13:22 minute for redis/MDS/pricing/api-gateway (F13/F19/F31/F43), and the identified cause (13:22:10Z) demarcates rather than lags it; within-minute log ordering varies by seconds and no rival needs a different ordering. Alternatives were tested, not dismissed: H3 refuted by flat exchange-gateway/upstream metrics (p99 ~131ms, error 0.2%, upstream ~120ms, CPU ~30%) with no pre-13:22 onset (F25-F30); H2 refuted by flat MDS request_rate 910-1026 req/s with no 13:22 step (F36) and by a discrete data-loss signature load cannot produce; H4 ruled out by dependency graph and a ~1h52m gap (F3/F5); H5 unfalsifiable and adds no mechanism. Two residual details cap confidence rather than block: the trigger of the PING timeouts (crash/OOM vs partition vs host fault) is unidentified, and the blast-radius asymmetry (order-service flat F45/F46 while api-gateway latency-only steps F43/F44) is unexplained — but neither names a different origin or fixes a different component, so both are secondary details of an established origin. Data quality is sound: the sole partial result was superseded by a non-partial retry (F8/F9); the missing keyspace metrics are permanently unavailable and are not used to infer anything; no healthy claim rests on a single metric.
